page: Microsoft Azure E128-64ds_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V with dedicated CPU resources. Built as a constrained vCPU configuration of the larger Edsv6 footprint, this instance exposes 64 vCPUs alongside 1024.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core allocation of 16.0 GB per vCPU. The underlying compute infrastructure is powered by Intel x86_64 processors, and the instance operates without discrete hardware acceleration, featuring zero GPUs.

The instance includes 7559 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. This extensive direct-attached NVMe capacity operates as low-latency ephemeral scratch or cache space, complementing the machine's primary memory profile. In terms of licensing economics, restricting the vCPU count to 64 while maintaining the full 1024.0 GB memory envelope allows database deployments constrained by per-core software licensing models to maximize addressable RAM and local I/O capacity without incurring unnecessary software license overhead.

Because the server lacks discrete accelerators and complimentary public IPv4 addressing, all network traffic relies on internal virtual network routing and explicitly assigned connectivity. Azure E128-64ds_v6 is structured primarily for large in-memory databases, enterprise transaction processing systems, relational database instances requiring constrained core counts for licensing reasons, and memory-intensive analytics pipelines relying on high-capacity local NVMe caching.
description: Microsoft Azure E128-64ds_v6 is a memory-optimized x86_64 virtual machine executed on Microsoft Hyper-V, deploying 64 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel processor architecture. Operating with a constrained core profile, it provides 1024.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation of 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture includes 7559 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD space for high-throughput, low-latency temporary storage, while hardware graphics acceleration is absent with zero GPUs provisioned. The server provides a high memory-to-CPU ratio that benefits database systems subject to per-core licensing restrictions, enabling organizations to balance compute, substantial memory footprints, and heavy local scratch storage without paying for unused processor capacity. The instance is structured for high-capacity in-memory databases, large-scale relational workloads, data warehousing, and intensive caching setups.
